newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia unions, employers sign new wage accord.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia unions, employers sign new wage accord.

text.p: Slovenian employers and a majority of the country's labour unions on Monday signed a new collective agreement on work benefits aimed at putting a lid on excessive wage growth.
The accord will replace the previous agreement, which was introduced in 1990, renewed in 1993 and expired at the end of May.

"The agreement brings Slovenia closer to European Union standards and we expect it to increase the international competitiveness of Slovenia's companies," Samo Hribar Milic, project manager of the Chamber of Commerce, told Reuters.

He said the accord would slow down the pace of salary growth, since in future salaries would only be increased by a maximum of 85 percent of the retail price inflation rate, compared to a full rate increase under the previous deal.
Unions agreed to sign the accord only after employers said they would raise the basic monthly gross salary in the country to 59,150 tolars ($375) from 57,000 tolars previously.
Despite the accord, the government faces the threat of this year's second major railway strike.

Railway unions, demanding a 14 percent increase in wages and a 70 percent rise in holiday pay, have threatened to strike from Wednesday should another round of negotiations with the government later on Monday fail. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
